general_information.Description: '-Objective: By the end of the course, students will learn the basic knowledge of photography include: + Foundational history of photography. + Visual language and aesthetics of photography. At the end of the course, students will be able to: + Complete an final album including story, style, composition, lighting, concept and aesthetics values + Have many practical experiences. - Description: In this course, students will learn about: Foundational history of photography; Classification of photography. Greatest photographers; Structure of camera; Camera operation; Foundational composition and visual language of photography; Handling post-production; Aesthetic in photography.
general_information.StudentTasks: '- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose. - Promptly access to the FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the history and theory of photography, the relationship between photography and visual disciplines, and its influence on culture.

Understand both advanced digital and analog camera operations with the understanding of formats, exposure in photography, depth of field, shutter speed, and illustrate proper placement of plane of focus.
Illustration of advanced visual literacy skills by utilizing sophisticated compositional properties and visual qualities of a photographic image

Demonstrate the ability to recognize and control both natural and studio lighting with emphasis on the quality, quantity, direction of light and the resulting effect of light on the photographic image, and ability to determine what type of studio lighting equipment is necessary to properly light various types of objects, people, spaces, and locations.
Manipulate, manage, archive digital images and control the transition of image color, tone and value from screen to printed image.
Organize, edit, and evaluate a professional quality portfolio of photographic work that demonstrates creative problem solving skill and effective communication.
Having a positive attitude and a professional working style

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Student actively participate in class and making Portfolio; Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal

assessments.Question Type: Portrait Photography: Applying Camera Operation and Studio Lighting Techniques
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge: Understanding of cameras, studio lighting equipment and accessories, and principles of composition and portrait lighting. Skills: Ability to operate a DSLR camera and to apply studio lighting setups flexibly for portrait photography.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Set up studio lights, accessories, and camera settings 2. Select subjects and apply appropriate lighting 3. Capture, select, and edit images 4. On-site submission
assessments.Note: Submission file: - Original images (RAW), edited images (JPG). - Submit in class In-class work: - Execute in class

assessments.Question Type: Visual Storytelling: Meeting Technical, Compositional, and Content Requirements; Demonstrating the Ability to Organize Images into a Narrative
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge: Understanding how to organize captured images into a coherent and meaningful visual story. Skills: - Proficient operation of the camera. - Ability to capture motion effectively and apply natural light flexibly under varying weather conditions.
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Project registration 2. Project analysis 3. Photography session 4. Submission of images and review 5. Supplementary shooting 6. Organizing images into a narrative 7. Online submission
assessments.Note: Submission file: - Project document: topic, explaination (.docx) - Photo outline (.docx) - Original images (RAW), Image Organization and Storytelling File (jpg). - Submission online In-class work: - Project review

assessments.Question Type: Presentation: Demonstrating Research Skills and Knowledge of Photography History, with Focus on an Assigned Photographer
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Knowledge of Photography History, with Focus on an Assigned Photographer Skills: - Research and Presentation Skills - Skills in Using AI for Research and Presentation
assessments.Grading Guide: 1. Receive research topic 2. Group work organization: assign research and presentation tasks to each member 3.Slide submission 4. Presentation and Q&A
assessments.Note: Submission file: - Slide (pdf or pptx). - Development step or AI Usage report (pdf or docx). In-class work: - Presentation - Peer and instructor feedback on the presentation.
